subject: Recap + k6 onboarding: SLO targets, test accounts, and allowlist
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@veridian.ai>, Veridian AI SRE <sre@veridian.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: SLO targets & next steps from today's call

Alexandra / team — thanks for the time today. Short post-call recap and the asks that will help your SRE team run the customer-led load tests against our staging environment.

What we captured on SLOs (please confirm):
- p95 latency target (text-gen sync): <= 180 ms
- Sustained throughput: 120 requests/sec across the pooled endpoint (60/minute per virtual user shape)
- Streaming: 40 concurrent streams, median throughput ~6 kb/s per stream, target first-byte < 220 ms
- Error budget: < 0.2% 5xx during the test window

Planned customer-led test items:
1) k6-based scenario to exercise a mix of short and long contexts (0–2k tokens / 2–8k tokens).
2) A streaming pass to validate connection handling for your client; this requires a different routing policy on our side.
3) IP allowlist and a temporary test account (scope-limited) from Redwood for the staging endpoints.

Action items and owners:
- Veridian: confirm preferred test window(s) and provide SRE contact(s) (name + cell).
- Redwood (Rishi): share k6 scenario, runbook, and IP ranges to allowlist; provide temp token and instructions for token rotation post-test.
- Redwood (Camila): stand by for on-call during the test for troubleshooting and log access.

Attachments: proposed_slo_matrix.csv (baseline values for SLOs we discussed)

Thanks — let me know if I missed anything.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.m@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@veridian.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian AI SRE <sre@veridian.ai>
Date: 2026-05-23T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: SLO targets & next steps from today's call

Thanks Rishi — helpful recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- Preferred test windows: next Tue 2026-05-26 02:00–05:00 UTC or Wed 2026-05-27 22:00–01:00 UTC. We can do either; prefer Tue if Redwood prefers earlier.
- SRE contacts: Marco Silva (marco.silva@veridian.ai) and Linh Tran (linh.tran@veridian.ai). Marco will lead the execution.
- Streaming: yes, we want to run a streaming pass. We'll exercise both short-lived and long-lived streams.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you provide a scoped test token (no production data) and confirm the exact hostnames and ports for staging?
2) Please send the IP ranges we must allowlist and any NAT egress notes.
3) Can you share the k6 script and the expected ramp profile so we can align our traffic generators?

We'll also attach our internal run window approval once the calendar is confirmed.

Thanks — Alex
Alexandra Ruiz
Director, Product Operations | Veridian AI
alex.ruiz@veridian.ai | +1 (650) 555-3321

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@veridian.ai>, Marco Silva <marco.silva@veridian.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-23T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: SLO targets & next steps from today's call

Alex / Marco — good plan. We can support the Tue 2026-05-26 02:00–05:00 UTC window. Details below and attachments included.

1) Staging endpoints and test account:
- Host: staging-api.redwood.ai
- Port: 443 (TLS)
- Temporary test token (scope-limited): TOKEN_TEST_VRD_20260526 (expires 2026-05-30T23:59:00Z) — use only for the staging host above.

2) IP allowlist ranges (egress from Veridian):
- 18.214.12.0/24
- 34.89.128.0/22
- 52.14.200.0/23
Notes: If your team sits behind a NAT pool, please provide the public egress IPs so we can add precise entries.

3) k6 assets and runbook: Attached is redwood_k6_runbook.md which includes the recommended scenario (mix of short/long contexts), ramp-up (30m to 120 vus), steady-state 120 req/s target, and a streaming sub-scenario that opens 40 concurrent WebSocket connections for 30 minutes. The runbook also includes expected thresholds and the log paths we will watch.

4) Streaming specifics: to exercise our streaming path, set Content-Type: application/stream+json and include the header X-Redwood-Mode: stream-test. We will route streaming traffic to a dedicated pool; please note the latency metrics are captured differently (first-byte, connection-establish) — see the runbook section "Streaming metrics".

5) Fallback and escalation: Camila will be on-call for infra-level issues and Soojin will monitor and help interpret server-side trace IDs.

Attachments included: redwood_k6_runbook.md, allowlist_instructions.pdf

Please confirm that the Tue window works for Marco's SRE team. Once you confirm, we'll create a brief canary (10% load) 30 minutes before the full run to validate connectivity.

Thanks — Rishi

Rishi / Camila — confirmed. Tue 2026-05-26 02:00–05:00 UTC works for our team. Linh and I will own the execution.

Notes from SRE:
- We'll run the canary at 02:00 UTC for 30 minutes at ~12 req/s to validate token/allowlist/connectivity.
- Full ramp begins at 02:40 UTC, target steady-state 120 req/s; streaming pass at 03:30 UTC for 30 minutes with 40 concurrent streams.
- We will exercise a 2k token prompt and one 8k token prompt variant to cover both tails.

Request: please provide CloudWatch/Datadog temporary viewer link or a short-lived log bundle access so our on-call can correlate trace IDs. Also confirm the exact header for the streaming flag (you mentioned X-Redwood-Mode: stream-test).

Acknowledged attachments: redwood_k6_runbook.md, allowlist_instructions.pdf. We'll pull the k6 scripts from the Drive link this afternoon and do a dry run tomorrow afternoon in our dev lab.

Thanks — Marco
